info.title: gpt-image-2.6 API
info.description: Create image tasks using AI models with support for multiple models and parameter configurations

post.description:
- GPT Image 2.6 (gpt-image-2.6-sunburst / gpt-image-2.6-flare) supports text-to-image, image-to-image, image editing and markup-guided editing, with animated GIF and SVG vector output
- Asynchronous processing: use the returned task ID to [query the task](/en/api-manual/task-management/get-task-detail)
- Generated image links are valid for 24 hours. Save the results promptly

model.description:
Image generation model name, with improved stability and control for commercial use

| Model ID | Best suited for |
|---|---|
| `gpt-image-2.6-sunburst` | Greater detail for precise visual work |
| `gpt-image-2.6-flare` | Faster generation for quick iteration |

Both models accept exactly the same parameters. Actual token consumption at the same `quality` tier may differ slightly; use the returned `usage` as the source of truth.

prompt.description:
Prompt describing the image to generate or how to edit the input image

**Length limits (both must be met):**
- Up to `32,000` characters (counted as Unicode code points)
- The `prompt` text itself must not exceed `60,000` bytes when encoded in UTF-8

Different characters use different numbers of UTF-8 bytes. Use the actual encoded byte count.

If either limit is exceeded, shorten the prompt before resubmitting.

**Recommendation:** If the prompt exceeds `8000` tokens, the generated image may not match expectations; shortening the prompt is recommended.
prompt.example: A beautiful colorful sunset over the ocean

image_urls.description:
Reference images as public URLs, for image-to-image and image editing

**Note:**
- Number of input images per request: `1~16`
- Size of a single image: not exceeding `50MB`
- Pixels of a single image: width × height not exceeding `178,956,970` px
- Side length of a single image: width / height each not exceeding `23170` px; exceeding this may cause errors
- Supported file formats: `.jpeg`, `.jpg`, `.png`, `.webp`
- Image URLs must be directly accessible by the server, or the image URL should directly download when accessed (typically these URLs end with image file extensions, such as `.png`, `.jpg`)
- In image-to-image / image editing scenarios, the reference images themselves also incur additional image input token consumption
- With `markup_url`, markup applies to the first image and the others serve as references; the first image must have width × height ≤ `16,777,216` px
- Input reference images are not supported when `output_format` is `svg`

mask_url.description:
Inpainting mask URL — marks the region of the reference image to regenerate. **Only valid in image edit mode** (must be combined with `image_urls`); the mask is silently ignored in pure text-to-image requests.

**Format requirements:**
- **Must be a PNG with an alpha channel**: transparent pixels (`alpha < 255`) = regions to regenerate; opaque pixels = preserved
- **Mask dimensions must exactly match the reference image dimensions** (width × height in pixels)
- Single mask per request

**Note:**
- At least one reference image is required in `image_urls`; a mask sent alone has no effect
- Cannot be combined with `markup_url`
- Common errors:
    - `Invalid mask image format - mask image missing alpha channel`: the uploaded image has no alpha channel (JPEG, opaque PNG, etc.). Re-export the mask as a PNG with transparent regions.
    - `Invalid mask image format - mask size does not match image size`: the mask dimensions don't match the reference image. Resize the mask to the same pixel dimensions as your reference image.

markup_url.description:
Public URL of a markup layer. Use circles, arrows or freehand marks to indicate what to change in the reference image, and describe the changes in `prompt`. **Only valid in image editing mode** (requires `image_urls`).

**Format requirements:**
- **Must be a PNG with transparent pixels**: draw only the annotations and leave the rest transparent. Do not draw directly on the original image
- **Dimensions must exactly match the first reference image** (width × height in pixels)
- The first reference image and the markup layer must each have width × height ≤ `16,777,216` px
- File size: no more than `50MB`

**Note:**
- Markup applies to the first image in `image_urls`; the remaining images serve as references
- Cannot be combined with `mask_url`
- Supports standard image and GIF editing, but not SVG
- Can also be supplied as `model_params.markup_url`; the top-level value takes precedence when both are present
- In `prompt`, also specify what to preserve, for example, "keep everything else unchanged and remove the red circle"

size.description:
Generated image dimensions. Defaults to `auto`. Standard images and the intermediate image used for SVG generation share the following rules; GIF uses the separate rules in section ④.

**① Standard images / SVG intermediate image: ratio format (15 options)**

- `1:1`: Square
- `1:2` / `2:1`: Extreme portrait / landscape
- `1:3` / `3:1`: Ultra portrait / landscape (3:1 limit)
- `2:3` / `3:2`: Standard portrait / landscape
- `3:4` / `4:3`: Classic portrait / landscape
- `4:5` / `5:4`: Common social media
- `9:16` / `16:9`: Mobile / desktop widescreen
- `9:21` / `21:9`: Ultra-wide

**② Standard images / SVG intermediate image: explicit pixel format**: `WxH` (or `W×H`), e.g. `1024x1024`, `1536x1024`, `3840×2160`

- Both width and height must be multiples of `16`
- Each edge range: `[16, 3840]`
- Pixel budget: `655,360 ≤ width × height ≤ 8,294,400` (about 0.65 MP ~ 8.29 MP)
- Aspect ratio: `≤ 3:1`

**③ Standard images / SVG intermediate image: `auto`**: The model decides the size automatically (`resolution` does not apply in this mode)

**④ GIF output**: `size` specifies the dimensions of each frame. Only `auto` and explicit pixel dimensions are supported, not ratios.

- With `auto`, each frame is `512×512`
- Explicit frame width and height must be positive multiples of `16`
- The `655,360` minimum pixel count for standard images does not apply to individual GIF frames; for example, `512x512` is valid
- The image combining all frames must satisfy the edge, total pixel and aspect ratio limits; see `model_params.frame_count` for grid layouts and per-frame limits
- `resolution` does not apply

**Out-of-range handling:**
- For standard images and SVG intermediate images, a ratio + `resolution` combination that exceeds the budget is automatically scaled down proportionally (e.g. 4K 2:1 → 3840×1920)
- Explicit GIF frame dimensions that exceed the limits return HTTP 400 and are not automatically scaled down

resolution.description:
Resolution tier shortcut, only effective when `size` is a ratio; ignored in explicit pixel mode and for GIF output

**Pixel budget rules** (dimensions are derived from the target pixel count and the `size` ratio, aligned to multiples of 16):

- `1K`: ~1 MP (1024² = 1,048,576 pixels)
- `2K`: ~4 MP (2048² = 4,194,304 pixels)
- `4K`: ~8.29 MP (3840×2160 = 8,294,400 pixels, the maximum)

**Landscape / square output dimensions** (portrait dimensions are the landscape width/height swapped, e.g. `2:3` = `3:2` reversed):

| Ratio | 1K | 2K | 4K |
|---|---|---|---|
| `1:1` | 1024×1024 | 2048×2048 | 2880×2880 |
| `2:1` | 1456×720 | 2896×1456 | 3840×1920 \* |
| `3:1` | 1776×592 | 3552×1184 | 3840×1280 \* |
| `3:2` | 1248×832 | 2512×1680 | 3520×2352 |
| `4:3` | 1184×880 | 2368×1776 | 3312×2480 \* |
| `5:4` | 1152×912 | 2288×1824 | 3216×2576 |
| `16:9` | 1360×768 | 2736×1536 | 3840×2160 (UHD) |
| `21:9` | 1568×672 | 3136×1344 | 3840×1648 \* |

\* Marks combinations that are auto-downscaled to fit the pixel budget. Values are case-insensitive.

quality.description:
Rendering quality, which directly affects output token count and cost. Defaults to `medium`

| Value | Output tokens (1024²) | Relative image output cost (1024²) |
|---|---|---|
| `low` | 824 | ~0.57× |
| `medium` | 1,449 | 1.0× |
| `high` | 1,756 | ~1.21× |
| `xhigh` | 3,122 | ~2.15× |
| `max` | 7,024 | ~4.85× |

**Note:**
- This table compares image output costs only, excluding input costs and SVG authoring model costs
- Calculated for `1024×1024`; output tokens vary with total pixels and aspect ratio. Use the returned `usage` for actual consumption
- For GIF output, tokens are calculated for the combined image containing all frames; for SVG output, this setting applies to the intermediate image
- Use `low` for quick drafts. For final assets, compare tiers to balance detail, latency and cost

complexity.description:
Planning depth before image generation, independent of `quality`. Defaults to `high`

- `low`: Suitable for local changes such as replacing a background or changing sign text
- `medium`: Balanced
- `high`: Suitable for text-heavy images, complex layouts or complex relationships between objects

**Note:**
- Higher levels take longer and may introduce unwanted changes; compare results for your task
- Changing `complexity` does not incur an additional charge
- For SVG output, this setting applies to the intermediate image
- Can also be supplied as `model_params.complexity`; the top-level value takes precedence when both are present

background.description:
Alpha channel of the output image. Defaults to `opaque`

- `opaque`: Flat background, no alpha channel
- `transparent`: Keeps the alpha channel

**Note:**
- `transparent` is a Preview feature and results may be unstable
- When using `transparent`, `output_format` must be `png` or `webp`
- When `output_format` is `gif` or `svg`, only `opaque` is supported

output_format.description:
Output file format. Defaults to `png`

- `png`: Lossless, supports transparent backgrounds
- `jpeg`: Lossy compression with smaller files
- `webp`: Balances file size and quality; also supports transparency
- `gif`: Animated GIF; see `model_params` for frame count and frame duration
- `svg`: SVG vector image, suitable for logos, icons and other graphics that need to scale without losing quality

**Note:**
- When `background` is `transparent`, only `png` or `webp` is allowed
- `gif` supports both text-to-image and image editing
- For `gif` or `svg`, `n` must be `1`
- `svg` only supports text-to-image
- SVG generation first creates an intermediate image, then uses an authoring model (`model_params.svg_model`) to convert it into SVG. Tokens consumed by the authoring model are billed separately at the selected model's rates
- The SVG result is a static vector file without scripts, external resources or embedded raster images
- For SVG output, prompts with substantial text or complex layouts take longer and may require around 2 minutes

n.description:
Number of images to generate, each billed independently

**Note:**
- Text input tokens scale linearly with `n`
- Support for `n > 1` is currently unreliable: even with a value greater than 1, only one image is often returned. The actual count is whatever `results` holds in the response, and billing follows the returned `usage`. If you need several images, send multiple single-image requests instead
- When `output_format` is `gif` or `svg`, this must be `1`

model_params.description:
Model-specific parameters. GIF frame parameters and SVG authoring parameters must be supplied in this object.

- `frame_count` and `frame_duration_ms` are only allowed with `output_format=gif`
- `svg_model` and `svg_reasoning_effort` are only allowed with `output_format=svg`
- Parameters incompatible with the output format return HTTP 400; they are not silently ignored

frame_count.description:
Number of GIF frames. Only available when `output_format` is `gif`. Defaults to `9`.

All frames are generated together as one combined image. Explicit frame width and height must be positive multiples of `16`; individual frames are not subject to the minimum pixel count for standard images. Edge lengths below are in pixels.

| Frames | Per-frame limits | Example size |
|---|---|---|
| `2`~`8` | ≤ 1,036,800 pixels; one edge ≤ 960, the other ≤ 1920 | `960x1072` |
| `9` | ≤ 921,600 pixels; both edges ≤ 1280 | `1280x720` |
| `10`~`12` | ≤ 691,200 pixels; one edge ≤ 1280, the other ≤ 960 | `960x720` |
| `13`~`16` | ≤ 518,400 pixels; both edges ≤ 960 | `720x720` |

**Grid layout (columns × rows):**
- `2`~`8` frames: `4×2` or `2×4`
- `9` frames: `3×3`
- `10`~`12` frames: `3×4` or `4×3`, with `4×4` tried if necessary
- `13`~`16` frames: `4×4`

**All of the following must also hold:**
- At least one layout must keep each edge of the combined image ≤ `3840` px, total pixels ≤ `8,294,400` and aspect ratio ≤ `3:1`
- When using a `4×4` layout, each frame must satisfy the area and edge limits listed for `13`~`16` frames
- If no available layout fits, the request returns HTTP 400; the area and edge limits in the table are not the only constraints

With `size=auto`, each frame is `512×512`, which works for every supported frame count. Output tokens are calculated for the combined image, not by adding up individual frames.

frame_duration_ms.description: Duration of each GIF frame in milliseconds. Only available when `output_format` is `gif`. Defaults to `200`, rounded to 10-millisecond increments

svg_model.description:
SVG authoring model that converts the intermediate image into SVG. Only available when `output_format` is `svg`. Defaults to `gpt-6.1-terra`

**Note:**
- Tokens consumed by the authoring model are billed separately at the selected model's rates
- The task result's `usage` includes `svg_model`, `svg_input_tokens` and `svg_output_tokens`
- Authoring model input and output tokens are listed separately and are not included in `usage.total_tokens`
- At task creation, credits for `2,000` input and `8,000` output tokens are reserved for the authoring model. On completion, billing is adjusted to actual usage: unused credits are refunded and any shortfall is charged

svg_reasoning_effort.description:
Reasoning effort of the SVG authoring model. Only available when `output_format` is `svg`. If omitted, the authoring model's default level, `medium`, is used

| Authoring model | Allowed values |
|---|---|
| `gpt-6.1-terra`, `gpt-6-sol`, `gpt-6-luna` | `none`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` |
| `gpt-6.1-sol`, `gpt-6-astra` | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` |

**Note:**
- Reasoning tokens count toward the authoring model's output tokens

callback_url.description:
HTTPS callback address after task completion

**Callback Timing:**
- Triggered when task is completed, failed, or cancelled
- Sent after billing confirmation is completed

**Security Restrictions:**
- Only HTTPS protocol is supported
- Callback to internal IP addresses is prohibited (127.0.0.1, 10.x.x.x, 172.16-31.x.x, 192.168.x.x, etc.)
- URL length must not exceed `2048` characters

**Callback Mechanism:**
- Timeout: `10` seconds
- Maximum `3` retries on failure (retries after `1` second/`2` seconds/`4` seconds)
- Callback response body format is consistent with the task query API response format
- Callback address returning 2xx status code is considered successful, other status codes will trigger retry

status.description: Task status. Queued and running tasks both return `processing`; the final status is `completed` or `failed`.

can_cancel.description: Whether the task can be cancelled

Usage.description: Reserved credits at task creation. Query the task after completion for actual consumption and token details.

billing_rule.description: Billing rule. GPT Image 2.6 is billed per 1,000 tokens. Image usage, text input and SVG authoring model usage are charged separately at their respective rates.

bearerAuth.description:
All APIs require Bearer Token authentication.

**Get API Key:**

Visit [API Key Management Page](https://evolink.ai/dashboard/keys) to get your API Key

**Add to request header:**
```
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY
```
